name: kql-multi-hop-endpoints
description: Multi-hop endpoint handling that kql-multi-hop does not reach: a *literal* concept matcher as the far endpoint (rather than a bound variable), and a lower bound on a node that is also reachable by a shorter path. Both are cases where a traversal can silently ignore half the pattern.
setup: UPSERT { CONCEPT ?t { {type: "$ConceptType", name: "Node"} SET ATTRIBUTES { "description": "Graph node" } } CONCEPT ?p { {type: "$PropositionType", name: "links_to"} SET ATTRIBUTES { "description": "Directed edge" } } }

UPSERT { CONCEPT ?d { {type: "Node", name: "D"} } CONCEPT ?c { {type: "Node", name: "C"} SET PROPOSITIONS { ("links_to", ?d) } } CONCEPT ?b { {type: "Node", name: "B"} SET PROPOSITIONS { ("links_to", ?c) } } CONCEPT ?a { {type: "Node", name: "A"} SET PROPOSITIONS { ("links_to", ?b) ("links_to", ?d) } } CONCEPT ?x { {type: "Node", name: "X"} } }

cases.name: a literal far endpoint constrains which starts qualify
an unreachable literal far endpoint yields no solutions
a literal far endpoint on the reverse walk constrains the objects
a lower bound keeps a node reachable at that depth by a longer path
a lower bound past every path length still empties the set
